statement: Let S = { (points[i][0], points[i][1]) | 0 <= i < len(points) }. Let minX be the minimum x over all (x,y) in S and maxX the maximum x over all (x,y) in S. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = true iff for every (x,y) in S the pair (minX + maxX - x, y) also belongs to S.
preconditions: 1 <= len(points) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(points), len(points[i]) = 2; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(points) and j = 0 or j = 1, -100000000 <= points[i][j] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever is_reflected(points) returns r and is_reflected(q) returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Both points and q satisfy the input constraints: their lengths are between 1 and 10000, every point has length 2, and all coordinates lie between -100000000 and 100000000. Also, q is obtained from points by inserting or deleting copies of points, so the set { (points[i][0], points[i][1]) } equals { (q[i][0], q[i][1]) }.

statement: Let S = { (points[i][0], points[i][1]) | 0 <= i < len(points) }. Let minX be the minimum x over S and maxX the maximum x over S. Whenever the function returns true, for every integer y such that X_y = { x | (x,y) belongs to S } is nonempty, if m_y = min(X_y) and M_y = max(X_y), then m_y + M_y = minX + maxX.
preconditions: 1 <= len(points) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(points), len(points[i]) = 2; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(points) and j = 0 or j = 1, -100000000 <= points[i][j] <= 100000000.
